approved: Timor Sea Maritime Boundaries Treaty Consequential Amendments Bill 2019
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that partially implements a 2018 treaty establishing permanent maritime boundaries and a shared petroleum development regime between Australia and Timor-Leste.

The bill would amend the Seas and Submerged Lands Act 1973 to create a special regime area for the Greater Sunrise gas fields, where Australia and Timor-Leste jointly exercise sovereign rights and manage petroleum activities.
The treaty's special regime will remain in force until the Greater Sunrise fields are commercially depleted, and the bill provides for the regime area to end when the regime ceases.
Amends Commonwealth legislation to reflect new permanent maritime boundaries.
Establishes the Greater Sunrise special regime area in Australian law.
Gives domestic effect to treaty provisions on joint governance, environmental protection, vessels, and criminal law matters.
Allows Timor-Leste's petroleum authority to act as the Designated Authority for day-to-day regulation.
Creates a Governance Board with one Australian and two Timorese representatives.
Establishes a Dispute Resolution Committee to hear matters referred by the Designated Authority, Governance Board, or Greater Sunrise Contractor.
Australia and Timor-Leste, their governments, and entities involved in petroleum development in the Timor Sea, particularly the Greater Sunrise fields.

The government introduced the Timor Sea Maritime Boundaries Treaty Consequential Amendments Bill 2019 to implement the 2018 Australia–Timor-Leste maritime boundaries treaty, replacing previous Timor Sea arrangements and establishing the Greater Sunrise Special Regime Area. The bill also transitions the Joint Petroleum Development Area to Timorese jurisdiction, creates new international offshore areas for pipelines, and amends affected petroleum titles and legislation.

The speaker moved the second reading of the Passenger Movement Charge Amendment (Timor Sea Maritime Boundaries Treaty) Bill 2019, which amends the Passenger Movement Charge Act 1978 to impose the charge on journeys to installations in the special regime area, partially implementing the 2018 Australia–Timor-Leste maritime boundaries treaty.

The speaker argued for the Timor Sea Maritime Boundaries Treaty Consequential Amendments Bill 2019, noting that Australia had previously used bullying tactics in negotiations with Timor-Leste, and that the new treaty, achieved through conciliation under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, ends over 40 years of maritime boundary uncertainty and will enable development of the Greater Sunrise gas field.

Labor supported three bills implementing the Timor Sea Maritime Boundaries Treaty, which resolves a 40‑year maritime dispute and establishes new petroleum revenue arrangements—royalties from the Timor Sea funded over 95% of Timor‑Leste’s budget in 2016.

The speaker supported the three Timor Sea Maritime Boundaries Treaty bills, stressing the need for passage before East Timor's 30 August independence celebrations and acknowledging Labor's role in shifting Australia toward a rules-based settlement of the long-standing maritime boundary dispute.

The speaker argued the Timor Sea Maritime Boundaries Treaty corrects Australia's historical bullying and exploitation of Timor-Leste, referencing a 2002 incident where Alexander Downer allegedly bullied Prime Minister Mari Alkatiri. The speaker urged the passage of the bill to rectify past wrongs, including Australia's complicity in Indonesia's 1975 occupation and unfair resource sharing.

The speaker argued that the Timor Sea Maritime Boundaries Treaty Consequential Amendments Bill 2019 corrects a historical wrong and supports Timor-Leste, a poor and oil-dependent neighbour, by recognising extended maritime boundaries and establishing new arrangements for petroleum development and revenue. The speaker noted that the treaty, concluded on 6 March 2018, was delayed by the government's focus on political stunts rather than national interest, and commended the Opposition Leader and Prime Minister for planning to travel to Timor-Leste to finalise the agreement.

The speaker supported the Timor Sea Maritime Boundaries Treaty Consequential Amendments Bill 2019 and related bills, arguing the new treaty reflects Australian values of fairness and international law, and commended the joint development of the Greater Sunrise gas fields with Timor-Leste. They noted personal shame over past Australian treatment of Timor-Leste and praised the 2016 change in Labor’s position under Tanya Plibersek.

The Timor Sea Maritime Boundaries Treaty Consequential Amendments Bill 2019 implements the 2018 treaty with Timor-Leste, transferring the Joint Petroleum Development Area and adjacent areas to Timor-Leste's jurisdiction and establishing transitional arrangements for petroleum activities, including new offshore areas for the Bayu-Undan and potential Greater Sunrise pipeline corridors.
